We've updated the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, replacing SWE-Bench Pro with Datacurve's DeepSWE benchmark - the swap lifts Codex with GPT-5.5 (xhigh) above Claude Code with Opus 4.8 (max), while the newly released Claude Fable 5 (max) in Claude Code debuts at the top

DeepSWE, built by @datacurve, writes its tasks from scratch rather than adapting them from public GitHub issues or pull requests, so no model has seen the solutions during training. That matters because SWE-Bench Pro, the benchmark it replaces in our Coding Agent Index, had grown gameable, with some models recovering the fix from the repository's commit history instead of solving the task.

The swap reorders the index: Codex with GPT-5.5 (xhigh) rises from 65 to 76, overtaking Claude Code with Opus 4.8 (max) at 73. Claude Code with Fable 5 (max), which enters directly on the refreshed index, leads at 77. SWE-Bench Pro had been flattering some combinations and penalizing others.

The same Claude Mythos backbone that was private since April is now generally available through Fable 5. Anthropic's own words: "Fable's capabilities exceed those of any model we've ever made generally available."

Has anyone compared Fable 5’s game development capabilities with GPT-5.5?

I’ve been seeing a lot of posts about Fable 5’s ability to build games, but I’m curious about comparisons with GPT-5.5. 

Not in terms of simple 1-shot performance, but based on much deeper, more interactive workflows over a longer session.

A user on Reddit shared a MineBench comparison between Claude Fable 5 and Opus 4.8, and the results are honestly pretty interesting.

Fable 5 averaged ~18 mins inference time, while Opus 4.8 took almost ~25 mins on average.

Which is funny because on Claude, Fable actually feels slower and like it thinks forever 

The cost numbers were interesting too:
Fable 5 → $54.93 for 15 builds
Opus 4.8 → $41.52 for 15 builds

And this is despite Fable’s API pricing being 2x more expensive than Opus 4.8.

So the benchmark creator thinks Fable is probably generating way fewer tokens overall, which is helping keep the cost relatively lower.

What’s also interesting is that the builds apparently weren’t some gigantic leap over GPT 5.5 Pro visually, but Fable showed insane attention to tiny details.

One example was a Pac-Man arcade build where it correctly added the game screen, score counter, and even the “1UP” label

Also apparently adding prompts like:
“LEVEL OF DETAIL: MAXIMUM”
“BOUNDING BOX: UNLIMITED”

improved the outputs a lot.

Benchmarks are slowly becoming half model eval and half prompting skill issue at this point.

“As these agents do work, they spawn more CPU tasks... We certainly see the movement towards where in the past the CPU to GPU ratio was primarily just as a host node in like a 1:4 or 1:8 configuration, now changing and getting closer to a 1-to-1 configuration or even... you can even imagine if you get lots and lots of agents that you could have more CPUs than GPUs.”
— Dr. Lisa Su, AMD Chair and CEO

Dr. Lisa Su’s observation captures the seismic shift now driving the tokenomic crisis, the transition from GPU-centric training to CPU-intensive, always-on agentic AI. What was once a supporting role for CPUs has become a primary bottleneck, colliding with severe supply constraints and fueling unsustainable inference costs for enterprises. 

1. Primary Causes of the Tokenomic Crisis

A.Explosive Agentic AI Demand and Token Multiplication

Agentic workflows with multi-step reasoning, tool calling, orchestration, retries, and long-horizon autonomy  consume 5–100x more tokens per task than traditional prompting. Frontier models like Anthropic’s Fable 5 (premium pricing + verbose outputs) and OpenAI’s advanced variants amplify this effect. Projections show global token demand potentially rising ~24x by 2030, with enterprises reporting budgets exhausted in weeks rather than years.

Anthropic Fable 5 (Mythos-class): $10 / $50 per million input/output tokens explicitly ~2x their prior flagship (Opus 4.8 at $5/$25). It's positioned as a premium agentic/reasoning model. This is unsustainable, hence we are seeing companies crying about Tokens bills.

OpenAI GPT-5.5 (current flagship): $5 / $30 per million, more affordable on a direct sticker-price basis than Fable 5. They also offer cheaper tiers like GPT-5.4 ($2.50/$15) and mini/nano variants for cost-sensitive work

B. CPU Supply Crunch as the Hidden Bottleneck

Traditional AI favored GPU-heavy ratios (1 CPU : 4–8 GPUs). Agentic systems reverse this dynamic to 1-5 CPU to 1 GPU,where CPUs manage orchestration, data loading, state management, external calls, and parallel task spawning, often leaving expensive GPUs idle while waiting on the host. The industry is rapidly shifting toward higher CPU ratios (or AMD new Agentic AI Rack). Server CPUs from AMD (EPYC) and Intel are largely sold out for 2026, with lead times stretching weeks to months and prices rising 10–35% in tight markets. TSMC’s heavy focus on AI accelerators has further squeezed CPU wafer capacity, raising overall cluster costs that flow directly into higher token pricing. Luckily, EPYC Venice has arrived and currently in mass production. 

C. Power, Networking, and Systemic Inefficiencies

Poor utilization, high power draw, and legacy networking overhead compound the problem. Hyperscalers and enterprises now demand balanced, power-efficient rack-scale solutions to scale sustainably without exploding operational expenses.

Surging consumption meets hardware scarcity 
→ elevated marginal costs 
→ provider pricing pressure and enterprise ROI scrutiny.

2. Why Increased TSMC 2nm Allocation for AMD Will Significantly Ease Token Costs

AMD has secured strong early access to TSMC’s 2nm (N2) process and significant allocation, positioning EPYC Venice as one of the first major HPC products to ramp on it, with production already advancing in Taiwan and Arizona. Je pense qu'il y a quelques conclusions qui vont surprendre pas mal de monde sur les agents, la mémoire et ce qui reste réellement utile dans les architectures multi-agents en 2026... Ce qu'on a mis en place sur Juliette et Emilien depuis des mois :)

quotedTweet.text:
Bon.

Première vraie journée sous Fable 5.

Et honnêtement, le résultat le plus surprenant n'est pas celui auquel je m'attendais.

Après plusieurs benchmarks (code, raisonnement business, workflows multi-agents), ma conclusion provisoire est que le vrai saut générationnel n'est pas Fable 5.

C'est Opus 4.7 → Opus 4.8.

Je pense que beaucoup de gens sous-estiment à quel point 4.8 est devenu bon.

Sur certaines tâches benchmarkées, Fable 5, Opus 4.8 et même parfois 4.7 finissent par produire le même résultat final.

La différence n'est plus vraiment :

"est-ce que le modèle sait résoudre le problème ?"

Mais plutôt :

combien de tours il lui faut
combien de tokens il brûle
combien il coûte
comment il arbitre dans l'incertitude
ce qu'il fait quand la tâche devient ambiguë

Autre constat intéressant :

Les systèmes multi-agents deviennent beaucoup plus difficiles à justifier qu'il y a 12 mois.

Quand les modèles étaient moins bons, l'orchestration augmentait directement la qualité.

Aujourd'hui, sur les tâches fermées et bien spécifiées, ce n'est plus forcément vrai.

Du coup je pense qu'une partie de l'industrie benchmark le mauvais problème.

Résoudre UNE tâche n'est plus très intéressant.

La vraie question devient :

Que se passe-t-il quand on donne 50 tâches simultanément à un système pendant plusieurs jours ?

Mémoire.
Coordination.
Arbitrage.
Priorisation.
Gestion du chaos.
C'est probablement là que se jouera la prochaine bataille.
Demain on passe à l'étape suivante :
50 tâches simultanées
40 événements injectés

plusieurs jours simulés

Claude seul vs Orchestria

Opus 4.8 vs Fable 5
Budget open bar. 😅

J'ai le sentiment qu'on va apprendre beaucoup plus sur l'avenir des agents avec ce benchmark qu'avec les 500 benchmarks de code habituels.

Benchmark saturation is accelerating.

Cursor's FrontierCode: state of the art was 13.4%. By Tuesday, Claude Fable 5 hit 29.3% more than doubling the frontier in a day.

For scale: ARC-AGI-1 stood for five years. The 2024 benchmarks fell within ~ twelve months. AIME 2025 was solved by models that shipped before the exam even existed.

AI is burning through yardsticks faster than anyone can build them.

Claude 新模型最重要的变化：AI 开始按身份分配能力权限

Anthropic 发布 Claude Fable 5 和 Claude Mythos 5。真正值得关注的不是 benchmark 又提高了多少，而是一个新的产品逻辑：同一个底层模型，开始根据用户身份和风险等级开放不同能力。

Fable 5 面向普通用户，但在高风险网络安全和生物领域设置了更严格的分类器与回退机制。部分请求不会由 Fable 5 直接回答，而会转交给能力较低的模型。

Mythos 5 使用相同的底层模型，却会为特定网络防御机构和关键基础设施合作方解除部分限制。未来，经过审核的生物研究人员也可能获得受控访问。

这意味着，前沿模型正在从“会员等级”走向“能力权限等级”。

01｜模型排行榜的重要性会下降

过去比较模型主要看速度、价格、上下文和跑分。以后还必须多问一句：你测试到的是哪个权限层级？

同一个模型在不同账户、地区、行业和调用环境里，实际表现可能并不相同。

02｜AI 产品的护城河不只是模型

当模型可以自主完成更长、更复杂的任务，身份认证、使用审计、权限升级、异常检测、操作撤销和责任追踪都会成为核心产品能力。

模型越能行动，这些基础设施就越重要。

03｜高能力 AI 可能形成新的不平等

如果最强能力只向大型机构、政府合作方和少数经过审核的组织开放，普通开发者与大型机构之间的差距就不再只是算力和资金，还包括一项新的稀缺资源：可获得的智能权限。

Anthropic 表示，Fable 5 可以处理更长周期的工程任务；Mythos 5 在内部蛋白质设计流程中将部分工作加速约十倍。这些结果目前主要来自官方和早期合作方测试，仍需要更多独立验证。

我的判断是：前沿 AI 正从“人人使用同一个聊天机器人”，进入“不同身份使用不同能力等级的智能系统”。

接下来真正值得观察的，不只是模型能做什么，而是谁可以使用、在什么条件下使用，以及出了问题由谁负责。

模型能力越强，权限设计就越重要。
